Rust binding gap evaluation: all 259,828 recorded calls retained; 32,414 local targets and 227,414 unresolved. Candidate-only global label matching partitions the unresolved population into 90,529 zero / 37,939 single / 98,946 multiple candidates and produces 9,778,507 pairs. Exact package + lexical owner + method matching gives 6,373 single candidates, still unverified.

The typed receiver control compiled and ran (`3:999`); MIR distinguishes `Vec::<u8>::len` from `Domain::len`, while native extraction leaves both targets NULL. The real frozen `labels!` fixture has zero generated `label` bodies before compiler expansion and one afterward; all 14 compiled label outputs match. This establishes one declarative-macro control, not workspace/procedural-macro coverage.

Extension MCP observed managed DuckDB 1.5.5 separately; experiments used pinned native DuckDB 2.0.0 with the approved extension. No runtime upgrade, source-graph mutation or candidate promotion. Source-sampling OOM was corrected by materializing 12 narrow keys before joining source blobs under the same 1GB cap.

Evidence and reproducible scripts: `/Users/kevintruong/project/SpurCode/docs/research/artifacts/2026-11-15-rust-binding-gap/`. Report: `/Users/kevintruong/project/SpurCode/docs/research/2026-11-15-rust-binding-gap.md`. Independent evidence review is pending.
